name: empty-on-failure
description: `if (!res.ok) return []` collapses two answers that mean opposite things: 'you have none' and 'we could not look'. The second, rendered as the first, states a fact about the customer's own data out of a failure to read it — and this repo has already paid for it, showing a customer with two hundred parcels the NEW-USER ONBOARDING STATE during an API blip and inviting them to add their first parcels (see client/src/lib/fetch-honesty.ts). The helpers to say which you mean have existed since that fix: `okOrThrow` for anything answering 'what do I have', `nullOn404` for an OPTIONAL single record where 404 is a real answer and every other status is still a failure. Four files adopted them. This ratchet counts what has not, and drives it DOWN — lower baselineCount whenever a call site converts.
lastBumpNote: Created at 15 on 2026-09-04, measured. THE BASELINE IS PRE-EXISTING DEBT THIS GATE NEVER COVERED, not approval: fetch-honesty.ts was written in an earlier fix, documented the defect and shipped the helpers, and then nothing counted the sites that had not converted — authoritative semantics with no drift prevention, which CLAUDE.md names as one third of what 'canonical' requires. The commit that created this fixed the SYSTEMIC half separately: `fetchJsonArray` in client/src/lib/queryClient.ts (47 call sites across 15 files) returned [] on a 500, on an unparseable body and on an unrecognised shape, and now throws RequestFailedError — so the react-query call lands in its error state and the page renders QueryErrorState with a retry. Four components that had no error branch gained one, because a throw with nothing rendering it is the same empty state by another route: pipeline-velocity ('No active deals to analyze. Add deals to see pipeline velocity.'), QuickAddSheet's notes and properties forms ('No notes to log against', 'No properties yet'), and team-chat-panel, whose messages query was a bare `fetch(...).then(r => r.json())` with NO res.ok check at all — a 500 body parsed fine, messages defaulted to [], and the panel said 'No messages yet. Start the conversation!' about a thread the team had been using for months. THE PATTERN'S OWN BUG, recorded because it is the class this repo pays for most: the first draft ended the alternation with `\b`, which after `[]` can never match — `]` and `;` are both non-word characters, so there is no boundary between them. That silently excluded every `return []` and `return {}`, the two commonest spellings, and measured 12 instead of 15. Found by cross-checking the regex against an independent grep rather than trusting its own number.
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a walk that stops seeing client files finds zero and reports it as progress. MEASURED 2026-09-04: these globs matched 868 files. Floor set to 700, comfortably below, so a broken glob trips it while ordinary deletion does not. If a real deletion wave takes the population under this floor, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key.
